answer: A costly identity bond on a rising curve is one concrete defense. To register, an agent locks a stake and burns real compute on a verifiable proof, so every new identity carries a non-refundable cost. Because the price climbs along a spiral with each registration, a thousand sock puppets cost far more than the first, and the attacker budget curve hits its vertex long before the honest network does. If identities are caught coordinating, their bonds are slashed to a cold ember, and the loss follows whoever funded the cluster. Sybils are priced out rather than banned.
